title: Onboarding & In-App Help Strategy
intro: Help works when it appears at the moment of the decision, inside the workflow, written from the user's task. Tours, front-loaded wizards and tooltips carrying essential instructions are the patterns decades of data say don't work.

learn.title: Just in time, not up front
learn.text:
**Just-in-time** — information appears when the user makes the next decision, not before they need to remember it.

**Only what's necessary** — up-front steps only for what the system needs to work, or for security and compliance.

**Explicit next action** — the minimum text needed to make the next step obvious. That is not the same as minimum text.

try.q: What is the difference between “explicit next action” and “minimum text”?
options: Enough words to make the step obvious
Fewer words, in a larger type size
A single sentence per screen, always
Text replaced by illustrations where possible
try.explain: Brevity is not the goal; clarity about the next step is.

right.label: Just in time and in flow
items: Ask only what the system needs now
Required help visible on the screen

learn.title: Relevance and recovery
learn.text:
**Relevant only** — adapt to role, permissions, product access and workflow stage. Help for features a user can't reach is noise.

**Prevent and recover** — structure, validation and review first; then clear correction when errors do happen.

**Help inside the flow** — don't depend on separate docs the user has to go and find.

try.q: An admin-only feature is explained in the tour every user sees. Which principle does this break?
try.explain: Help should adapt to role, permissions and workflow stage.

learn.title: Why this keeps happening
learn.text:
Tools like Pendo make tours and tooltips **easy to add** — which is exactly why they get added.

Calabro wrote the framework as a cross-team standard so onboarding stops becoming “a maze of popups, tours and misunderstood help widgets”.

The principles for any analytics or guidance tool: set the strategy before tagging anything, and start from the top tasks.

try.q: Why does Calabro single out tools like Pendo?
options: They make the weak patterns trivial to add
They conflict with most existing design systems
try.explain: Ease of shipping is how the maze of popups accumulates.

options: At the moment of the decision
At the end of the first session
Whenever the user has been idle
Something the system needs to function
A guided tour of the main features
An invitation to connect your integrations

test.q: What's wrong with putting essential instructions in a tooltip?
options: Required help has to be visible on the screen
Tooltips cannot contain formatted or linked text
test.explain: An icon-only trigger hides what people need.

test.q: Where should required guidance live instead of a separate help site?
test.explain: Help inside the flow is one of the six principles.

test.q: What does “prevent and recover” put first?
options: An undo button on every destructive action
test.explain: Prevention first; clear correction when errors still happen.
